pr_title: Make DirectoryInfoWrapper better handle missing directories
pr_body:
EnumerateFileSystemInfos tries to noop when root directory does not exist
but the directory might be deleted between the time it checks Exists and
begins enumerating.  The value for Exists might also be stale as it is cached.

issue_context.title: DirectoryInfoWrapper throws DirectoryNotFoundException when directory is deleted during enumeration
issue_context.body:
### Description

Reported here https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/44626
Discovered here https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/41426#issuecomment-694985134

I thought I had rooted out this issue and solved it by reducing the timer period(and added an extra test to try and capture the issue), but now I suspect there is a codepath here that is creating the timer on a background thread even when the PFW is disposed.  So the polling timer is still going then we later delete the directory from under it. 

The delete is happening between these two lines, and causing the exception:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/5c65d891f203618245184fa54397ced0a8ca806c/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.FileSystemGlobbing/src/Abstractions/DirectoryInfoWrapper.cs#L36-L38

We could just catch the exception here, since it's already trying to avoid it by checking Exists.  I was hoping to find a better fix to identify where to cancel the timer.  Perhaps we are canceling the timer but it was already running?

This should fix PollingFileProviderShouldntConsumeINotifyInstances to be less flaky.

The delete is happening between these two lines, and causing the exception: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/5c65d891f203618245184fa54397ced0a8ca806c/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.FileSystemGlobbing/src/Abstractions/DirectoryInfoWrapper.cs#L36-L38 We could just catch the exception here, since it's already trying to avoid it by checking Exists. Author: ericstj
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-Extensions-FileSystem`, `untriaged`
Milestone: -

I believe this is indeed a race condition.  The Timer gets disposed by https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/5c65d891f203618245184fa54397ced0a8ca806c/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.FileProviders.Physical/src/PhysicalFilesWatcher.cs#L261 but nothing will stop a currently running timer callback when this happens.

The problem can occur if a directory is deleted after the exists check and before enumeration starts here: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/5c65d891f203618245184fa54397ced0a8ca806c/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.FileSystemGlobbing/src/Abstractions/DirectoryInfoWrapper.cs#L36-L38

If the deletion happens during enumeration the enumeration will halt, but if it happens at the start an exception is thrown.  We can address this by handling the exception, since the existence check makes it clear that this should ignore missing directories.
Here's a customer hit on this same race condition: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/54830949/omnisharp-not-functioning-properly-in-one-project-but-is-in-another

> but nothing will stop a currently running timer callback when this happens

I've not read the full description to know whether this is relevant,  but there are Timer.Dispose{Async} overloads that let you wait until all work associated with the timer has quiesced.
I can safely say that it's part of the DirectoryInfoWrapper's contract to not throw on a missing directory regardless so I feel this is the right fix.

> there are Timer.Dispose{Async} overloads that let you wait until all work associated with the timer has quiesced.

We'd need to add DisposeAsync to PhysicalFilesWatcher to support this, but that's not a bad idea.  I'll open an issue on it.

review_comments:
> _Confirmed the behavior that we only throw on the root handle_

If I'm getting this correctly, from your comment in the main section, we only expect an exception if specifically the root is not found? It won't happen if a subdirectory is the one that disappears while enumerating?

> It won't happen if a subdirectory is the one that disappears while enumerating?

Correct, I linked to the places in DirectoryInfo that handle these cases and differ for subdirectories of a call to enumerate.
Any idea why this test was marked as OuterLoop in the first place? Or asking a different way: Why did you decide to remove it?

I added it, then marked it that way because it started failing in CI I wasn't sure if the issue was due to system load, since this test case does create hundreds of timers.  I investigated and found that it's not load, but a race condition.  Timers uses a single thread and just adds to a collection, so it scales, but more timers create more work for that thread to [handle](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/162b33e19eb5a3434867541be691e1082039b130/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Threading/Timer.cs#L122).  We have a lot more chances to hit that race condition due to the number of timers which is why this was showing up in CI.
